findings.text: the three vocabularies use a token-keyed double-nested shape (fast: / two-space fast: <definition>), not the root-keyed entry shape with a definition field that section 5 names (the shape physical_bases.yml `bases:` and locus_registry use). The deviation is forced and documented: the codegen token extractor (grammar_codegen/spec.py _extract_vocab_tokens) recognises a root key only for loci, carriers, bases, operators and axes, so a `populations:` root key would extract as the single token 'populations' and break the generated enums and the drift gate, and tests/grammar/test_vocab_uniqueness.py reads a bare mapping's keys as its token list. Adopting the plan's shape needs a one-line change to that tuple in spec.py, a method outside this node's write scope. Recorded rather than repaired: the loaders return the same sets, load_zones the same ordered tuple, and test_vocab_uniqueness.py and test_codegen_drift.py pass at head.

_entry_definitions opens the vocabulary file and calls yaml.safe_load itself instead of reusing _load_yaml (vocab_loaders.py:33), which section 2 of the plan names as the registry's YAML reader and which an earlier review already required another loader to fold into. The duplicate read is three lines and its only added behaviour is the missing-file guard, which can be kept ahead of a _load_yaml call.

the plan's done-when asks that each test fail with its mechanism removed; the recorded control removes only the emission (definitions=definitions_applied dropped from the AppliedConventions construction) and reddens the two rendering tests, leaving test_loaders_return_the_recorded_token_sets, test_definitions_carry_a_population_a_zone_and_an_aggregation and test_a_token_without_a_definition_loads_and_contributes_nothing green. Each of those three does name a condition under which it fails — dropping the all-dicts branch of _load_flat_token_list empties load_populations, and adding a definition to the core zone reddens the last — but none was exercised, so coverage of the loader-shape mechanism rests on reading, not on a recorded red.

the reviewed run's manifest records baseline_suite, after_suite and negative_control_log as prose (e.g. 'negative-control.log (2 failed, 3 passed, EXIT=1)') rather than the armed JSON shape and the bare log path the dispatch contract requires, so those fields cannot be parsed by an admission check even though the logs they name exist and agree with them.
